bull_bear.body:
- Centralized supply chain and 75%-automated Bhiwadi manufacturing enabling scale, lower cost and next-day delivery
- In-house frame and lens engineering and manufacturing (69.87% of prescription eyeglasses sold in FY25 made in-house facilities)
- Customer-focused in-house design (105 new collections launched FY25; 109-member design team)
- Lenskart brand and portfolio of owned sub-brands spanning economy to premium (India's Most Trusted Eyewear Brand 2025, TRA)
- Technology-first approach with AI virtual try-on, computer vision and geo-analytics
- Omnichannel retail platform of 2,806 stores plus 100mn+ app downloads
- Track record of revenue growth (32.52% CAGR FY23-FY25) and margin expansion
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material cost and supply concentration — Cost of raw materials consumed was 24.52% of total expenses in FY25; majority purchased on spot basis; significant frame/raw-material import dependence on China (incl. Baofeng JV).
- History of losses and negative cash flows — Restated losses in FY23 (Rupees 637.57 million) and FY24 (Rupees 101.54 million); profitability only recently achieved.
- Leased store network intensity — All retail stores and offices are leased; high lease liabilities, depreciation and finance costs; non-renewal/rent escalation risk.
- Dependence on Promoters and key personnel — Brand tied to Peyush Bansal's reputation; loss of key management could hurt operations.
- Acquisition integration — Growth relies on integrating Owndays, Dealskart, Stellio and Quantduo; synergy and goodwill impairment risk.
- Regulatory / FEMA and ED inquiry — Ongoing Enforcement Directorate inquiry under FEMA and denied ODI NOCs; pending DPIIT Press Note 3 approval.
- Competition from unorganized retail — ~77% of India prescription eyewear by value is unorganized, constraining pricing power.
- Manufacturing concentration — Almost all lens cutting/edging concentrated in the Bhiwadi-Gurugram cluster; disruption risk.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Lenskart designs and sells prescription eyeglasses, sunglasses, contact lenses and eyewear accessories under its own brands and sub-brands through an omnichannel network of websites, mobile applications and 2,806 stores globally (2,137 in India, 669 international as of June 30, 2025). It runs a centralized supply chain with in-house frame and lens design and manufacturing at Bhiwadi (Rajasthan) and Gurugram (Haryana), supplemented by facilities in Singapore and the UAE.

risks.note: Increasing participation from organised and unorganised players across markets. Management's stated mitigation is the vertically integrated model with structural cost and speed advantages, plus brand pull that reduces dependence on promotional spending.

Currency volatility, inflation and consumption slowdowns across markets. Management points to the essential, medical nature of prescription eyewear as natural demand resilience, 42% international revenue as currency diversification and backward integration to absorb input cost pressure; the MD&A separately flags Rupee devaluation raising the import bill, logistics and raw material costs, and notes the fashion element of the business is more exposed in a slowdown.
risks.risk: Macroeconomic fluctuations - currency, inflation and consumption slowdown

risks.note: Dependence on specific manufacturing hubs and import corridors. Mitigation cited is multi-site manufacturing (Bhiwadi, Hyderabad, Thailand JV), progressive backward integration and RFID-enabled inventory visibility.

Risk of inconsistent customer experience as the store network scales rapidly. Mitigation is NPS-led feedback loops, AI-driven store operations, centralised training systems and self-service technology that reduces human variability.

Cybersecurity risks associated with customer data, facial recognition and AI systems; the BRSR separately identifies Data Privacy & Protection as a material risk where growing digital operations increase exposure, with breach costs, litigation, regulatory penalties and reputational damage as the stated financial implications.

Ability to attract, retain and develop specialised talent across geographies, mitigated through AI-enabled hiring, local-first international teams and an acqui-hire strategy. The BRSR discloses permanent-employee turnover of 51.4% in FY 2025-26 (53.9% in FY 2024-25 and 65.7% in FY 2023-24), a structurally high attrition rate for a workforce of 21,859 permanent employees globally.
risks.risk: Human capital - talent attraction, retention and high attrition

risks.note: Evolving regulations across 16 countries including data privacy, healthcare and trade policy. Mitigation is dedicated compliance teams per jurisdiction, proactive engagement with regulatory developments and diversified sourcing to mitigate trade policy risk.
risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance exposure across 16 countries

risks.note: Identified in the BRSR materiality table: climate-related regulations, carbon pricing and extreme weather events can affect operations and supply chains, with productivity losses and supply chain disruptions as the negative implication; the approach is renewable energy adoption, climate risk assessments and business continuity planning.
